title: 13-Week Cash Forecast & Covenant Runway — Meridian Building Group
scenario: The lender wants a 13-week (one-quarter) cash forecast with the borrowing-base review. Roll cash forward from the $642,300 quarter-end balance using the Q1 operating run-rate, scheduled debt service, and cash taxes, then test the trough against the $250,000 minimum-cash covenant. Assume new work is working-capital neutral over the period (new billings ≈ new collections), so operating cash approximates EBITDA.

exhibits.label: Q1 2026 operating run-rate (basis for the 13-week operating cash)
Week-1 stress: vendor payment run (from the AP aging workflow)

tasks.prompt: Compute the 13-week operating cash (EBITDA proxy): operating income plus the non-cash depreciation add-back.
tasks.explanation: 290,000 + 80,000 = 370,000. Depreciation is non-cash, so it is added back; working-capital changes are assumed neutral over the quarter.

tasks.prompt: Compute total cash debt service for the quarter (interest + scheduled principal).
tasks.explanation: 70,000 interest + 45,000 principal (180,000 ÷ 4) = 115,000 — the same debt service used in the DSCR covenant test.

tasks.prompt: Roll the forecast: starting cash + operating cash − debt service − Q1 cash taxes = ending cash after 13 weeks.
tasks.explanation: 642,300 + 370,000 − 115,000 − 46,200 = 851,100. Cash builds over the quarter under the run-rate.

tasks.prompt: Compute ending covenant headroom against the $250,000 minimum-cash covenant.
Stress the worst week: if the $282,000 vendor payment run clears in week 1 before collections arrive, what is the cash trough, and does it breach the $250,000 covenant?
tasks.explanation: 642,300 − 282,000 = 360,300. That is the low point and it stays $110,300 above the $250,000 covenant — no breach, even in the front-loaded-disbursement case.

tasks.prompt: Write a 4-5 sentence liquidity narrative for the lender.
tasks.explanation: Cash starts at $642,300 and ends near $851,100 after $370,000 operating cash, $115,000 debt service, and $46,200 taxes; the week-1 trough of $360,300 (after the $282,000 vendor run) stays above the $250,000 minimum-cash covenant, leaving $601,100 of quarter-end headroom and a comfortable runway.

outputArtifact: A 13-week cash forecast rolling from $642,300 to $851,100 (operating cash 370,000; debt service 115,000; taxes 46,200), a week-1 trough of $360,300, and $601,100 of covenant headroom vs the $250,000 minimum.

conversationSim.prompt: The lender asks: 'Do you stay above your minimum-cash covenant over the next quarter, even in a tight week?' Draft a 2-3 sentence answer.
conversationSim.modelAnswer: Yes — our 13-week forecast rolls cash from $642,300 to about $851,100, and even if the full $282,000 vendor run clears in week one before collections, the trough is $360,300, still $110,300 above the $250,000 covenant. We end the quarter with $601,100 of headroom after covering $115,000 of debt service and $46,200 of taxes.
